strengths: Write-ahead ledger, post-commit dispatcher, deterministic control owner, provider-neutral operator boundary, deny retention, and independent evaluator are explicit.
The proposal is structurally valid after a fully recorded interface-only repair.

findings.finding: dispatcher sends artifact-released/v1 to every consumer without typed subscriptions or projector rules, so irrelevant artifacts can trigger the wrong worker and stage transitions are not enforced by the control plane.
evidence-collector receives every released artifact, emits another ledger artifact, then receives that released evidence again; no exclusion or idempotency rule prevents an infinite evidence loop.
adapter-builder runs in the sandbox but its adapter artifact can reach composer without a separate verification decision proving the exact generated hash passed tests.
The slice omits planner, discovery, license inspection, probe scheduler, adapter verification, and composer while still claiming deny enforcement, candidate probing, and a system bundle.
The dispatcher broadcasts committed artifacts directly to workers; control-plane stage-transition decisions do not gate those releases, contradicting deterministic stage ownership.
policy-gate to ledger and dispatcher to policy-gate flows are duplicated, increasing ambiguity and the risk of repeated actions.

conclusion: Do not implement, benchmark, hybridize, or promote this proposal. It contains useful design ideas but no measured component strength and fails critical architecture gates.
